subject: gk
question: A housemaid gets her 12 - year - old daughter to help in her work as a house cleaner at a residential colony instead of sending her to school. Which fundamental duty is violated by the housemaid?

options.text: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child
To defend the country and render national service
To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence

solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide opportunities for education to his/her child**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• She **violates the fundamental duty under Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution, specifically 51A(k),
 
• It s**tates that it is the duty of every citizen to provide opportunities for education** to his or her child or,
 
 
• as the case may be, to work toward the achievement of the same.
 
 
 
• By making her 12-year-old daughter work as a house cleaner instead of sending her to school,
 
 
• the housemaid is neglecting her duty to ensure that her child receives an education.
 
 
 
• **Education is essential for the development and empowerment of children**,
 
• It is considered a fundamental responsibility of parents or guardians to facilitate this.
 
• This situation not only contravenes the fundamental duty of providing education but also raises concerns about child labor,
 
 
• which is prohibited under various laws in India, including the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A**

 
 
• **​Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution outlines the **Fundamental Duties** of citizens. 
 
• It was added by the **42nd Amendment** in 1976 
 
• It serves to remind citizens of their responsibilities toward the nation.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A enumerates **a set of **fundamental duties** that every citizen is expected to uphold.
 
• **Some of these duties include**:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
